It appears that there are less students using the crosswalk at Euclid and Colorado. I believe this is because of Newton’s
new location. When the school was at the corner of Arapahoe and Colorado, multiple parents would park at the
mortuary to pick up/drop off their students. This does not appear to be the case anymore. That being said, there are
still multiple students that do use the crosswalk. Obviously, the amount of students using the cross walk could change
from year to year based on student enrollment.
Traffic at the intersection of Arapahoe Rd. and Colorado Blvd. is congested and usually backed up during morning drop
off and afternoon pick. Also, there is a lot of student pedestrian traffic. If a fully controlled intersection is implemented
at Colorado and Euclid, I would like to limit the additional impact on the intersection of Arapahoe Rd. and Colorado
Blvd. (vehicles backing up to or through the already stressed intersection).
The concern I do have is for citizens accessing the stadium. There have been a few events at the stadium, and the
parking lot at Newton has filled up quickly. This forces patrons to park in areas around the school to access the
stadium. I believe the stadium is designed to hold 1,500 people. To insure the safety of the patrons crossing Colorado
Blvd, I hope the intersection is well lit for night time events.
Ideally, I would like an elevated pedestrian bridge across Colorado Blvd. I do understand that this is an unlikely option
based on location and budget. A fully controlled intersection would increase the safety of school buses exiting the
school onto Colorado Blvd, traffic exiting Euclid onto Colorado Blvd, and pedestrians attempting to cross Colorado
Blvd, to attend and exit the stadium or Newton Middle School.

I provided a few feedback points regarding the Colorado & Euclid study, and unfortunately will likely be unable to
attend the public forum on Thursday.
One of my concerns is the survey itself in that I understand you are trying to determine where public interest is and
derive a priority, but the reality is that all of the items that are listed are important, and I would hate to see the city
interpret something that is ranked 'lower' as not important.
I think two of the largest issues overall are Child Safety and neighborhood impact. I live in Arapahoe Estates and have
a daughter that will end up going to Newton, so both of these are quite important to me.
I watch many children walk up Euclid every morning to go to school, and I not only see the lack of traffic control at
Euclid and Colorado, but also drivers that drive way too fast on Euclid trying to cut through, and I expect that to just
get worse as we have more games etc. at the stadium. Ideally you are diverting traffic in a way that doesn't make
cutting through Euclid an appealing option in the first place. If traffic flows well on Arapahoe and Colorado then there
is no need to find other routes. Similarly, if traffic is diverted before and after games that too can affect where people
try and drive.
Lastly, I know that a few years ago there was a study done on the Colorado corridor in general with a lot of emphasis
on reducing overall Colorado traffic. I would hope some of the ideas from that study are carried forward as well.
Happy to discuss more.
